parsed.use_case: A build automation tool or package manager validating a collection of software modules and their declared prerequisite libraries before compilation or installation. The system must confirm that no circular dependencies exist among components, which would otherwise result in an unresolvable execution deadlock.
system_examples: Terraform — analyzing resource configurations and reference attributes prior to creating an execution plan to detect mutually dependent resources
Bazel — evaluating target declarations and their declared prerequisites before compilation to ensure there are no circular dependency loops
npm — inspecting package manifests during dependency tree resolution to prevent unresolvable circular installation requirements
parsed.explanation: The problem is solved using topological sorting, implemented either through Kahn's algorithm (in-degree reduction) or depth-first search with node state tracking (cycle detection), running in O(V + E) time and space. A naive approach of independently tracing all reachability paths from every node can explode to exponential O(V!) time on dense dependency structures. In production build and orchestration systems, this validation is a critical static analysis step to prevent infinite loops, deadlocks, and costly runtime rollback failures.
